newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa descent as Sept fails at above 1,060.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa descent as Sept fails at above 1,060.

text.p: Cocoa futures drifted back to end Friday lower on long liquidation and pre-weekend profit-taking on the back of recent gains.
Traders said the sterling's strength against major units also did not help the situation.
"The technicals are getting stale, the market is losing an upward momentum and the recent short-covering and new buying also did not help," said one trader.
"It's a technical market. There's no fundamental aspect behind the move," he added.
Benchmark September made an early high at 1,063 stg a tonne, a slight progress from Thursday's peak of 1,061, before holding in the 1,050s at lunch.
But it lost further ground in the afternoon to end the day 15 down at 1,040 stg.
But traders said Friday's setback to below 1,950s did not signal that this week's run-up,after last week's sell-off,was over.
The chart picture would turn bearish if September failed to muster support at 1,000 stg.
Sterling powered above three German markets for the first time in 6-1/2 years on Friday as traders proved unable to resist the lure of higher British interest rates.
The pound rose to 3.0010 marks, the strongest it has been since October 1990. Against the dollar, it reached $1.6986, the strongest since January 10.
Volume reached 4,429 lots, centred on September contract.
